title: Hydroxychloroquine modulates the progression of experimentally induced benign prostatic hyperplasia in rats via targeting EGFR/ERK/STAT3 and AR/FOXO1/TRAIL pathways: computational and in vivo studies.
authors: El-Maadawy, Walaa H; Hafiz, Ehab; Tadros, Samer A; Fahim, Sally A; Ebrahim, Haidy M; Fouad, Marwa A; Attia, Yasmin M
one_liner_zh: 该文通过分子对接和动物实验研究羟氯喹对大鼠良性前列腺增生的治疗作用，涉及蛋白-小分子对接而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD模拟方法，与TF-DNA结合机制课题关联度低。
abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a prevalent progressive age-related disorder in men, yet its etiopathophysiology remains poorly understood. Current treatments like finasteride (Fin) have limited long-term efficacy, necessitating alternative therapies. Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ), a safe antimalarial agent, possesses anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and antiproliferative activities, however, its therapeutic effect in BPH has not been investigated. Accordingly, we examined its therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms, alone or combined with Fin, in testosterone-induced BPH in rats. In BPH-induced rats, HCQ markedly reduced prostate weight and index, and PSA, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, kappa and IL-6), and the transcription factor "NF-kappaB" levels, while improving histological abnormalities in epithelial and stromal tissues. HCQ reduced the mRNA expression of AR and ERK1/2, and decreased the protein levels of EGFR and STAT3. Additionally, HCQ increased the mRNA expression of FOXO1 and promoted apoptosis through both intrinsic and TRAIL-mediated pathways. This was evidenced by the upregulation of pro-apoptotic Bax and the downregulation of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 and Bcl-XL levels in the intrinsic pathway, as well as the reduction in mRNA expression of DR4 and DR5 in the TRAIL-mediated pathway. Notably, combining HCQ with Fin enhanced these effects. Molecular docking revealed HCQ's strong interactions with androgen receptor (AR), EGFR, ERK1/2, FOXO, and TRAIL death receptors (DR4/DR5), comparable to Fin except for STAT3. Our findings suggest that HCQ modulates BPH progression by targeting STAT3/FOXO1/TRAIL and EGFR/ERK/AR pathways, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for BPH, either alone or in combination with Fin.
abstract_zh: 良性前列腺增生（BPH）是男性中一种常见的进行性年龄相关疾病，但其病因病理生理学仍知之甚少。当前治疗药物如非那雄胺（Fin）的长期疗效有限，亟需替代疗法。羟氯喹（HCQ）是一种安全的抗疟药物，具有抗炎、免疫调节和抗增殖活性，然而其在BPH中的治疗作用尚未被研究。因此，我们在大鼠睾酮诱导的BPH模型中，单独或联合Fin，考察了其治疗潜力及潜在机制。在BPH诱导大鼠中，HCQ显著降低了前列腺重量和指数，以及PSA、睾酮、双氢睾酮、促炎细胞因子（TNF-α、κ和IL-6）和转录因子“NF-κB”的水平，同时改善了上皮和基质组织的组织学异常。HCQ降低了AR和ERK1/2的mRNA表达，并减少了EGFR和STAT3的蛋白水平。此外，HCQ增加了FOXO1的mRNA表达，并通过内源性和TRAIL介导途径促进凋亡。这通过内源性途径中促凋亡Bax的上调及抗凋亡Bcl-2和Bcl-XL水平的下调，以及TRAIL介导途径中DR4和DR5 mRNA表达的减少得以证实。值得注意的是，HCQ与Fin联合使用增强了这些效应。分子对接显示，HCQ与雄激素受体（AR）、EGFR、ERK1/2、FOXO和TRAIL死亡受体（DR4/DR5）存在强相互作用，与Fin相当，但STAT3除外。我们的发现表明，HCQ通过靶向STAT3/FOXO1/TRAIL和EGFR/ERK/AR通路调节BPH进展，为BPH提供了一种有前景的治疗策略，无论是单独使用还是与Fin联合使用。
